description:
PERF ROUND 43 member 1 (s513e, Opus, 2026-10-09): the split family (bench splitstrre 6.26x perl, splitcomma 3.20x, splitspace 1.74x at round 42's final table).

=== DONE (s513e) ===
Profile (base 462169f6, statprof): splitstrre -- cl-ppcre:split 74 % total, the generic SCAN dispatch per field (check-applicable-keywords, emf) and the minend wrapper, for a pattern that is one literal dot; splitcomma -- the generic CL SEARCH 53 % total (+ hairy data-vector-ref).  A non-literal regex split (`split /\s*,\s*/`) was measured already FASTER than perl (0.22 s vs 0.29 s), so the regex arm is untouched.
Fix (runtime only, cl/pcl-runtime.lisp): ONE dispatch on the pattern SHAPE, %p-split-shape -> :awk / :literal / :regex (ecase in p-split).  A pattern that is only literal characters -- a string with no metacharacter, or a regex (op or STRING) whose text is literal characters + escaped punctuation + \t \n \r \f \e \a with no /i /x -- is split by a typed (simple-array character) scan (%p-split-literal), perl's own fixed-string (fbm) path; a regex op's literal is computed once and kept in the new p-regex-match slot %split-literal.  Awk mode got the same typed scan (%p-split-awk); the result vector starts at 8.  Every shape answers what the engine would: a non-empty literal never matches empty.
Hand-replaced A/B (scratch/s513e/ab-m1.log, base core vs base + patch, best of 5, control +-1.1 %): splitstrre -77.6 %, splitcomma -59.0 %, splitspace -9.5 %, split(/\./) -76.0 %.
Probe table 40 rows (scratch/s513e/sprobe.pl): tree == base on all 40; 38 == perl; 2 documented divergences (`() = split` implicit limit -- not-supported.md; nbsp under /d).
Guard Pl/t/perf-levers-12.t rows 1-4 (shape mechanism, timed 600 000 literal splits < 1.5 s: 0.55-0.68 s here, 2.41 s on the base, 36-row answer table); inverse-verified on a 462169f6 extraction (rows 1 + 3 fail).
subject: PERF: split with a literal pattern (string or regex of literal characters) goes through cl-ppcre's split loop / the generic SEARCH -- splitstrre 6.3x, splitcomma 3.2x perl
